title: P0 Next Build UI: pure black/white fullscreen, theme and ALGO artifacts, PLAY/MIXER panel redesign
body:
## Hardware-owner Next Build UI correction — installed AQUORA 0.6.2

Owner reports that fullscreen ignores the chosen Black/White background, current themes need refinement, an anomalous line appears in the title next to **ALGO / page name**, the normal PLAY visualizer area shows a confusing **double panel / nested panels**, and MIXER panels look unfinished.

### Active acceptance checklist

- [ ] **Fullscreen background parity:** For **both Original and Polar Bloom**, the selected background applies to every fullscreen band. **Black must be exactly pure black `RGB(0,0,0)` / RGB565 `0x0000`; White must be `RGB(255,255,255)` / RGB565 `0xFFFF`.** Preserve geometry readability and color contrast on either selection. Do not force dark teal or tinted theme canvas. Honor the choice on return from fullscreen and across restart.
- [ ] **Improve all five themes:** Audit palettes across every screen for consistent legibility, clear focus/accent states, typography, color, borders and simple coherent panel styling. No overdraw or new expensive animation. Background Black/White setting overrides canvas color independently of theme.
- [ ] **Fix unexplained title line next to `ALGO` / page name:** Check the header's accent strokes, clipped overlong text, band boundaries, invalidated graphics and theme-specific rendering. Eliminate extraneous line artifacts without sacrificing an intentional readable layout.
- [ ] **Simplify normal PLAY visualizer:** Remove confusing nested/double panels around preview, present one clear visualizer region integrated with the rest of PLAY, preserve readable K1–K4 controls and exit/restore behavior. Visualizer remains hidden during startup intro (per updated #16).
- [ ] **Redesign MIXER panel layout:** Coherent eight-track console, focus-strip and bus pages without inconsistent double borders, clipped controls, meter artifacts, overlapping labels or poor spacing. Mute/solo, selected state, meter and Auto Level/Gain feedback remain accessible.
- [ ] Exercise **5 skins × 2 backgrounds × 3 fonts ×** major screens, both visualizers (normal/fullscreen), responsive transitions, start/stop and reboot persistence. Use authentic 240×240 host frame captures and pixel-level pure-black/white assertions. Audit under high mixer/visual load and ensure no increase in DSP load/XRUN.
- [ ] Preserve the last working sound engine, all eight roles and musical settings, bank migration, and live editing features. Physical FM-1 confirmation stays with owner.

### Source confirmation

In published `v0.6.2` `device/ui.c::draw()`, line ~535 currently sets:
```c
const uint16_t bg=artwork?RGB(5,17,22):ui_background?skins[ui_theme][1].canvas:RGB(0,0,0);
```
This forces **dark teal whenever fullscreen/intro artwork is shown**, regardless of selected Black/White. The current themed palette `skins[5][2]` also uses tinted dark/white canvases. Title rendering appears near lines ~736–765, with `ALGO` and current page name and additional bars/accents. The PLAY preview combines band content/panel framing; MIX has separate mixer_console/mixer_band paths. These are investigation starting points, **not assertions that every reported defect is already proven from software alone**.

Related: #2 discoverability, #10 fullscreen, #14 fullscreen restore, #16 themes/intro, #17 Polar Bloom cymatics, #20 one-press SAVE.

**State: OPEN — not implemented or verified.**

title: P0 Next Build: one-press SAVE from every page, even while playing, with clear bank confirmation
body:
## Next Build — critical owner request, November 5, 2026

**Hardware feedback:** AQUORA v0.6.2 is installed and running well so far, but the owner **could not figure out how to save a song**. The next build must make the dedicated **SAVE button usable at any time, including while music is playing**. No need to STOP or navigate into SETUP/Banks before saving.

### Required user experience (acceptance checklist)

- [ ] **One press of physical SAVE from any ordinary page (PLAY, SOUND, EVOLVE, MIX, DRUMS, SETUP, AIR, fullscreen)** captures and stores the current complete song/arrangement into the currently selected save bank (1–4). If the user has not chosen a bank, use a clearly indicated default, e.g. Bank 1. Save must work **whether transport is PLAYING or STOPPED**.
- [ ] **No hidden prerequisites** such as OCT− → Banks → K1/K2 → overwrite arm → STOP. Remove these from the *normal quick-save path*; keep a discoverable Banks page for explicitly selecting a destination, loading a bank, and inspecting saved slots.
- [ ] If the active bank already contains a save, pressing SAVE should update that bank in the same one-press workflow without a confusing arming requirement. Protect against incomplete/corrupt saves with an atomic write/CRC or a safe previous-good backup. Never silently lose the prior valid save on interruption.
- [ ] Show obvious on-device feedback: `Saving…` then `Saved to Bank N` (or an actionable failure message). Show the active bank and saved/unsaved status where practical. Do not imply success until durable persistence/verification actually completes.
- [ ] **Snapshot safety:** capture consistent state at a safe boundary and defer any blocking storage writes away from real-time audio processing. Never introduce audio crackle, xrun spikes, transport disruption, stuck notes or animation stalls.
- [ ] Save complete arrangement state (all eight role assignments and sounds, intentions, motifs, evolution, mixer/mutes/solos, drum kit/settings, Nature, FX, reference/binaural settings, locks, quantization, motion, etc. as supported by bank format). Confirm what is global vs per-bank. Keep backwards compatibility / migration for all existing four bank files and patch IDs.
- [ ] **Load/recall stays explicit**, does not accidentally overwrite during SAVE, and remains safe while playing (if load requires STOP, explain it on screen without blocking quick-save). New Song/Reroll must not steal the SAVE shortcut.
- [ ] Test SAVE from every page and fullscreen, with PLAY active and stopped, rapid repeated SAVE, all four banks, overwrite, restart persistence, migration from prior version, simulated power interruption/CRC failure and audio latency/stability. Ship concise on-device guidance plus updated manual.

### Evidence in shipped v0.6.2
[`device/docs/MANUAL.md`](https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/blob/v0.6.2/device/docs/MANUAL.md) currently states: **OCT− opens four arrangement banks; K1 bank, K2 Load/Save, K3 overwrite arm; SAVE executes only while stopped**. This directly conflicts with owner expectations.

**Status: OPEN / requested for next build.** Do not mark completed until behavior, persistence and software regression tests are verified. Physical FM-1 confirmation remains the owner's responsibility.

Cross-reference [Issue #2](https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/issues/2) for overall UI discoverability.

title: P0: All 19 AQUORA drum kits sound muffled — restore crisp attacks and distinct timbre without regressions
body:
## Actual FM-1 feedback — **ALL 19 DRUM KITS sound muffled**, not merely FM Moon Kit (v0.6.1)
The owner tested **every kit** and found similarly muffled/lacking attack/presence. Example: FM Moon Kit at **Density 8, HIT 95%, Level 100%** still sounds muffled. Do not limit the fix to that kit or assume high Density/HIT equals brightness/punch.

### Published v0.6.1 source evidence
- `device/dsp/engine.c::drum_sample()` uses exactly one shared kick, hand/snare and shaker architecture for **all 19 kits**. Kits change `kick, hand, shaker, root, skin, decay, brush`; FM kits (ID >=15) mostly switch a modest sine-based FM variant.
- Kick is dominated by a ~47–71Hz low-frequency sine with a small overtone and mostly slow natural-decay envelope. Hand transient is `tap*.64f + filtered_noise*.36f`; shaker uses high-passed noise. This architecture tends toward soft/dark timbres across *all* kits and may lack a sufficiently bright, transient attack layer, regardless of kit values.
- `drum_hit` is the probability of additional strikes on otherwise empty eligible subdivisions; **it does not increase per-hit attack/brightness**. `drum_density` controls placement/number of strikes; `drum_level` scales amplitude. The user expects higher punch/clarity, but these parameters do not supply that.
- Audio path includes user-level **Presence** only as a gain modifier (`1+(presence-50)*.006`), and global auto gain/auto level, a reverb/delay send, and master limiter. Trace **drum-specific frequency response, transients, routing, wet/dry, limiter gain reduction and gain staging** to identify other contributors to perceived muffling rather than presuming one specific cause.
- Keep low CPU cost: v0.6.1 initial flash default PLAY nearly 99% callback budget, later clean cold boot 83% Audio+FX and 0 XRUNs. No expensive FFT/reverb or multivoice sample playback without measurements.

### Mandatory remedies
1. Do **level-matched A/B analysis** for all 19 kits in isolation and in full generative mix, on headphones and onboard speaker where available. Render the kick, snare/hand and hats separately with spectral envelopes/attack times, transient peak/crest, masking, auto-level and limiting on/off, FX 0 vs normal. Find a shared bottleneck.
2. Retune shared kick/snare/hat DSP for noticeably clearer, stronger well-defined attack while preserving ambient softness: low-cost short noise/click onset, brighter and more natural snare/hand material, controlled high-frequency shimmer/hats, better multi-stage envelope / pitch sweep, more variety and separation between kits. Expose a **single DRUM TONE / BRIGHTNESS or PUNCH** parameter if needed (one canonical setting, directly labeled), separate from LEVEL, DENSITY and HIT.
3. Correct gain staging and masking with bass, piano, Nature and reverb. Don't just normalize/compress the entire mix louder or reduce all melodic sound. Preserve soft/high-dynamics presets; users should be able to make drums crisp when desired.
4. In DRUMS UI accurately explain and label **DENSITY = how many hits, HIT = optional-hit probability, LEVEL = volume, PRESENCE = drum mix emphasis**; don't pretend any of these is a brightness control. Add direct **per-kit audition** in context, and make kit differences obvious.
5. Add meaningful distinctiveness to all 19 kits, not variants of one muffled sine/noise mixture. Any new FM drum synthesis must be bounded and profiled per callback; preserve each existing kit name/ID and saved settings. When user selects FM Moon at 8/95/100, it must be audible and clear, not just louder or busier.
6. Compare per-kit and full-mix listening renders (old/new), transient and LUFS or equivalent level-matched playback, no clipping, no XRUN regression, 16 voice default-playback performance and long session. Owner physical-listening acceptance remains unverified until tested.
7. Preserve arrangement diversity, soft ambient intentions and ability to mute/solo; tests must cover across all 13 intentions and musical styles. No hidden extra per-sample processing when drums OFF.
8. Treat as release-blocking for next corrective version and retain rollback versions. 
Status: owner-observed all-kit issue, **not yet repaired**.

title: P0: Polar Bloom 2.0 — strongly audio-reactive intention/frequency cymatics-inspired geometry with bounded DSP cost
body:
## Owner v0.6.1 hardware feedback — retain visual design, greatly deepen musical responsiveness
"The second visualizer looks cool now", is going in the right direction, but the owner wants it to **react dramatically and continuously to the actual audio, selected intention, musical content and tuned frequencies**, visually inspired by the Japanese water-crystal / Masaru Emoto imagery. Maintain angelic, peaceful, beautiful identity, volumetric/2.5D depth, strong screen fill and slight downward centering previously requested. **Preserve the working Polar Bloom look** and enhance it, rather than reverting to the rejected horizontal ribbons or starting over.

### Source finding, published v0.6.1
`device/visual_worker.c::resonance_job()` currently makes 8 rings ×33 points, with `petals=3u+vis_input.frequency/300u`, `scene` affecting colors primarily, `bass` changing radius, drums and piano modifying ripples, choir changing a swell, and each track's meter scaling an amplitude. `device/ui.c::geometry()` draws ring connections with modest visual motion and color mainly selected by role. It reacts somewhat, but **intentions are not driving distinct evolving visual structure** and reference frequency only coarsely changes petals. This is not a rich audio-driven geometry generator. Also correct the Polar-only PLAY UI disappearing bug tracked in #14.

### Required design — artistic cymatics-inspired, not asserted scientific proof
- Treat Emoto-style water-crystal images as **visual inspiration**, not evidence that intention/frequencies scientifically change water or provide medical healing.
- **13 intention-specific coherent geometry/behavior profiles:** distinct symmetry, petal structure, branching, fractal-like crystalline lines, ripple propagation, mesh curvature, depth/tilt and color moods. Selecting a new intention must produce a visibly different yet coherent motif. Avoid cheap random geometric reshuffles; maintain beautiful stable motifs with gradual transitions.
- **Frequency-to-form mapping:** known selected Hz and 432/440 mode drive safe bounded phase/symmetry/interference/tension/halo characteristics. Ensure changing an actual frequency changes geometry deterministically, does not alias violently, and respects precise audio tuning. Frequency is an artistic mapping; no medical claims.
- **Real-time audio-driven modulation with clearly separable features:** bass and kick energize low-radius pulses/core/height; drum onsets send fast expanding ripples and spark points; piano/plucks articulate fine structures and harmonic flicker; pads/choir slowly expand/smooth petals and luminous halos; melodic pitch/motif/chord motion changes resonance/symmetry/rotation in a controlled musical fashion. Use real role meters, onset/event counters and cheap precomputed pitch/event metadata, or bounded aggregate envelope/band features when available. Don't fabricate FFT bins or expensive spectral capture.
- Add visible **attack → bloom → sustain → decay**; movement should respond to notes quickly yet retain graceful decay and naturally evolve as arrangement/intentions change. Distinguish genuinely audible onset/quiet/silence.
- Optional easy-to-find **REACTIVITY, COMPLEXITY and DEPTH** controls with safe presets (Calm / Dynamic) if performance allows. Control level sensitivity, response curve and visual density without altering audio. No duplicate/conflicting visual controls.
- Fullscreen remains edge-to-edge 240x240 with slight vertically lowered focus; PLAY embedded preview maintains complete controls for BOTH visualizers. Intro uses saved visualizer/theme preferences (#16).
- **Very strict audio stability priority:** v0.6.1 default PLAY already near 99% callback budget, 82 XRUNs/2s (#12). Audio feature telemetry must be cheap control-rate snapshots; no per-audio-sample FFT/per-pixel glow/expensive sin() or allocations in audio ISR; geometry only while visible per #15; reuse LUT, fixed bounded vertices, row stripes, no hidden worker dispatch. Simplify when CPU load is high rather than sacrificing audio stability.
- Test every intention and frequency in deterministic snapshots with representative audio note events; prove geometry really changes for intention/frequency and amplitude/onsets/motif; verify silence behaves correctly; A/B clips for dry/active 16-voice arrangement and no hidden CPU work. Native/single-core/emulator and physical delivered FPS + beauty verified by owner.
- Keep exact previous selection, settings migration and original visualizer unaffected. Complete next versioned corrective release once performance/audio are stable; not a cosmetic mock-up.

**Status: requested, not implemented; release-blocking to owner acceptance after default playback stability.**

title: P1: Persist selected visualizer for startup intro; ultra-lightweight refreshed UI with vibrant selectable themes
body:
## Owner request — corrective build after v0.6.1
1. **Remember which visualizer was selected** across power cycles and make AQUORA's ~10-second startup introduction display/animate **that selected visualizer**, not hardcoded Original. Both Original and Polar Bloom must work; future presets should use the same saved selection system.
2. Give the entire AQUORA UI a noticeably more polished, **extremely lightweight** visual appearance, with a few **distinct vibrant color themes**. Never add expensive layers, shaders, blur or background UI animation merely to change colors. Preserve the immediate editing/navigation fixes and audio stability.

## Confirmed source gaps (published v0.6.1)
- `device/app.c` persists only `motion[2]`, `perfect_key`, `lighting`, and `fps_auto` in `aq_settings` (`version=0x41513032`). **Visualizer selection is not globally saved**.
- `device/arrangement.c` includes `record->visual=visual_mode` for *individual arrangement banks*, but `arrangement_init()` resets `visual_mode=0` on startup. Loading a bank can restore it; ordinary selection followed by power cycling cannot be relied on to persist.
- `device/ui.c` intro calls `geometry(band*48)`, which is driven by the same `vis_output`; `visual_worker.c::prepare_geometry()` uses `visual_mode` for its variant. The persisted selection must be restored **before** the first intro geometry/paint.
- `device/ui.c` uses many hardcoded `RGB(...)` values and `static const uint16_t colors[SR_TRACKS]`. Refactor to **precomputed 16-bit RGB565 theme palettes**, not runtime per-pixel hue calculations.

## Implementation / UI design
### A. Persist and use visualizer choice
- Global **visualizer preference** changes when selected; persists without requiring a manual SAVE or bank save. Load it before `app_ui_init()` renders any intro/preview frame.
- Intro must render the **last selected Original or Polar Bloom** and use the saved UI theme; optional music-reactive dynamics can work where audio actually exists, but a silent intro must not need fake FFT/extra audio.
- Keep distinct **arrangement-bank visual** behavior predictable: define whether bank-load switches the active visualizer (currently recorded) and synchronize the global preference correctly; do not inadvertently replace a user's global selection when loading unrelated data unless explicitly chosen. Document visible semantics.
- Use one versioned, compact settings schema that migrates old v0.6.0/v0.6.1 settings without losing saved LED mode, motion, perfect-key, FPS, banks. Range-check unknown/corrupt values; safe fallback Original/legacy theme. Ensure atomic/low-wear writes or save-on-change/debounced/power-down mechanism appropriate to flash. No per-frame writes.
- Intro remains ~10s and instantly skippable on any knob/button/key without changing a setting or playing a surprise note. Preserve safe startup audio level and battery overlay behavior.

### B. Extremely lightweight UI refresh
- Introduce 3–4 selectable, vivid but readable **static RGB565 palettes**, plus existing AQUORA/Legacy styling. Suggested: **Aurora** (teal/violet), **Neon Lagoon** (cyan/magenta), **Solar Bloom** (coral/gold), **Midnight Prism** (indigo/electric blue). Final names/colors may be tuned for 240×240 screen visibility; user should perceive meaningful differences.
- Apply them consistently to main interface backgrounds, high-contrast text, knob focus/selection accents, SOUND and EVOLVE graphs, mixer meters and visualizer coloring/lighting accents as appropriate. Maintain track-role identity and mute/solo indicators. Theme should not change audio or nature/FX parameters.
- Prefer a **single canonical** `SETUP > DISPLAY > THEME` control and direct Quick Find entry. Avoid duplicate theme/edit controls in unrelated pages; UI shortcuts must point to the same setting.
- Make the whole UI easier to read and edit: crisp labels, clear selection highlight, comprehensible K1–K4 values, predictable navigation, minimal chrome and visual clutter, smooth but **event-driven** updates. This is a lightweight **visual design system**, not a heavyweight new UI framework.
- Do not consume any ongoing CPU when theme selection is not changing or screen visuals are hidden. Palette switch should update necessary dirty screen strips once, reusing existing fonts and geometry with cached colors.
- Maintain visible low-battery warning and battery fade when fullscreen. On fullscreen exit, restore entire PLAY UI and correct theme colors with no stale pixels.
- Add emulator 240×240 screenshots of all themes on PLAY, SOUND, EVOLVE, SETUP and INTRO, both visualizers; validate text contrast, edge cropping, no geometry redraw while hidden.

## Performance / safety gates
- Owner's real FM1 v0.6.1 defaults currently show ~97% audio+FX budget, callback mean ~5745 µs of 5805, ~82 XRUNs per 2 seconds and noticeable crackle (see [#12](https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/issues/12)).
- Visual polish must add **negligible CPU/memory overhead**; no dynamic allocations or expensive per-frame color math. Run matched A/B callback timings and zero-XRUN default PLAY tests. Cross-reference hidden-render gating [#15](https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/issues/15).
- Preserve [intro feature #8](https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/issues/8) and [canonical navigation #2](https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/issues/2). Avoid competing concurrent edits while Work is building.
- Tests: persistent selection across reboot, old settings migration, bank load, themes all combinations, boot skip, screenshot pixel checks, save-cycle write budget, session transitions, compile native/forced-single-core/emulator and hardware owner's visual acceptance.

## Status
New user requirement, **not yet implemented or tested**. Include in the next versioned corrective build; preserve released v0.6.1 artifacts and rollback.

comments.body:
## OWNER CLARIFICATION — themes must redesign the **panels and control surfaces**, not just recolor the current UI
Previous proposal of four accent palettes was liked, but the user specifically means **visually styled panels and such**: a cohesive instrument interface with crisp framed parameter groups/cards, lightly raised or inset control wells, obvious active/focus selection, elegant sliders, small meter windows, readable headers/footers, subtle separators and high contrast. Distinct themes should have **materially different panel looks and chroma**, not only global background/text color swaps.

**Recommended lightweight direction** for 240x240:
- Aurora: soft frosted teal glass-outline panels and violet highlights.
- Neon Lagoon: dark saturated panels with slim cyan/magenta neon edge accents.
- Solar Bloom: warm copper/gold recessed control panels and coral focus.
- Midnight Prism: angular blue/indigo instrument panels and bright electric outlines.
- Shared fixed 1px borders, 2px highlights, precomputed RGB565 fills and icon glyphs; use only existing line/rectangle/text primitives and partial 240x48 dirty-strip blits. No realtime blur, alpha, gradients, expensive bitmap assets, dynamic geometry, shadows per pixel or animations solely for chrome.
- Maintain crisp 240x240 layouts and visible readable labels/values, stable K1–K4 context, functional scroll/focus highlight; no duplicate settings or decorative chrome obscuring information. Theme applies to PLAY/SOUND/EVOLVE/DRUMS/MIX/AIR/SETUP/introduction; fullscreen remains artwork only except temporary battery indicator.
- Separate **panel skin** from **visualizer palette**, allowing selection of UI theme without inadvertently altering a selected visualizer's audio-reaction geometry or user setting.
- Benchmark themed UI vs legacy at default PLAY (currently XRUN failure): negligible CPU/flash/RAM increment, **no hidden theme workload**; prioritize #12/#15 default-playback audio regression before extra styling.
- Generate true 240x240 emulator screenshots of all panel treatments and test every parameter display and focus state, preserving saved selection and migration.
Status: clarified scope; **not implemented**.

## Owner late-add — persistent UI FONT SIZE choice (Small / Medium / Large)
Add a **single canonical `SETUP > DISPLAY > FONT SIZE`** control with exactly three clearly named user choices: **Small**, **Medium**, **Large**. Make it directly accessible through Quick Find as the same setting, without duplicate independent controls. Default to Medium (or migrate the current UI size to the closest unchanged default); save selection across power cycles and arrangement/bank loading without unrelated reset.

**Usability and 240×240 acceptance:**
- Scale **all user-facing UI text**, including section and panel headings, selected roles/patches, K1–K4 captions and values, DRUMS, SOUND/Instrument, EVOLVE, AIR, MIX, SETUP, battery/status indicators, confirmations and error messages; appropriately size focus boxes/panels and wrapping so fonts don't overlap or clip. Avoid scaling the entire canvas indiscriminately; adapt layouts and spacing for each size.
- Large must remain fully navigable and editable: prioritize essential parameters, use concise labels or intentional pagination, scroll accessible information rather than silently truncating necessary fields.
- Small should allow higher information density but remain crisp on the native LCD; Medium should be the default comfortable baseline. Show *live preview* of the size when changing, and preserve understandable navigation to switch back from Large.
- Theme-aware contrast; visualizer fullscreen remains immersive (fonts apply only to any shown labels/status). Intro wordmark/title may retain its art-directed size unless otherwise desired, while skip hints/menus must remain legible.
- Reuse/cache **existing bitmap glyphs or prebuilt font sizes**. No runtime vector rasterization, expensive resampling, dynamic allocation, or per-frame layout processing. Only rebuild text layout and dirty strips on size change; zero background cost when unchanged/hidden. Assess flash/RAM footprint of three bitmap sizes.

title: P0 real-time performance: zero hidden visualization/graph DSP and rendering workload
body:
## Owner mandatory performance directive
**Whenever a visualizer, animation or real-time SOUND/EVOLVE graph is not actually visible, it must consume no ongoing rendering/geometry/telemetry processing resources.** A single cheap active-view conditional is acceptable; the continuous hidden work is not. In the current physical v0.6.1 the audio budget is ~97–99% with frequent XRUNs, so this is P0.

### Verified 0.6.1 behavior to audit
- `device/app.c::app_frame` animates on `intro_active||page==PAGE_PLAY||page==PAGE_MIX||page==PAGE_SOUND||page==PAGE_EVOLVE` at ~20 fps even if visible page content is static or the SOUND category picker is on. Ensure **content visibility**, not page membership alone, controls animation.
- It correctly calls `prepare_geometry()` only on PLAY, but `device/ui.c::draw` can render the old `geometry` from other page fallbacks, sometimes for no useful reason. Review why/when visualizer geometry is required.
- `scope_track` changes to `SR_TRACKS` outside SOUND > Instrument graph, and `engine.c::render_samples` checks `scope_track<SR_TRACKS` before decimated capture. Keep this skip and optimize hot path so non-viewing avoids capture math/copies entirely (do not retain per-voice graph accumulation).
- `app_frame` unconditionally advances `evolve_history[64]` whenever transport steps change, even when EVOLVE graph isn't visible; this may be cheap but owner requests no continuous hidden graph bookkeeping; gate unless event history is required by musical engine. Do not disable **musical evolution** itself, which must continue sounding even when EVOLVE page is hidden.
- App init unconditionally calls `visual_init()`, `plat_cpu2_set(1)`; determine if worker can park safely when no visualizer graph is needed, without breaking audio or destabilizing core startup. No CPU2 worker dispatch or geometry while hidden; no hidden LCD rendering/blits.
- AIR radio/control, the main generative engine, its role meters for limiter/UX, LED output and audio effects must **not be turned off merely because their UI widgets are hidden**. Separate *audio-critical data* from optional visualization-only telemetry.

### Required implementation
1. One authoritative **visibility/consumer activation map**: intro visualization, PLAY embedded/fullscreen Original/new flagship, SOUND waveform/envelope/FX view, EVOLVE timeline, MIX meters, AIR sensor meter, debug/performance, hidden/static/setup. Only visible (and needed) modules may schedule graph/visual work; switching focus/picker/debug/fullscreen must update gates before next callback/render.
2. When a widget becomes hidden, immediately suspend its: geometry updates, graph sample capture, analysis/spectrum/band computations, per-frame animations/timers, ring-buffer/history writes for purely visual telemetry, worker submissions/waits, LCD strip blits and dirty-redraw requests. Keep minimal state needed for correct restoration only.
3. Sound engine and musical section evolution keep running regardless of UI view. Re-enable visual telemetry gracefully upon return without stale samples/ghosts. Respect fades on exit and full-screen battery fade; avoid stranded overlays, interrupt races and audio glitches.
4. Implement compiled/host counters for each module: **geometry jobs**, **graph samples captured**, **EVOLVE history updates**, **UI rendered frames and blits**, **CPU2 jobs/waits**, **inactive per-frame processing**, **audio/FX timing**. In hidden-state soak tests, optional graphics/telemetry counters must remain ZERO (except one-time transitions), and no visual-only DSP work in the 44.1 kHz callback.
5. Compare audio callback mean/p95/p99/max and XRUN delta at identical stimuli with each graphic mode ACTIVE vs HIDDEN, including SOUND picker, EVOLVE off-screen, FULLSCREEN on/off, debug, display static and different page transitions. Target measurable reduction and no 16-voice crackle; do not infer delivered FPS from submitted blits.
6. Keep animations attractive and responsive **when actually visible** at optimized bounded rates. Allow static screen to redraw only when state/values change; no pointless 20 fps animation. Use dirty 240×48 strips where practical. No avoidable background CPU/GPU/radio work.
7. All state cleanup/visibility transition tests, native and forced single-core, host emulator, audio regression, actual FM1 performance evidence owner verified. Don't fake gains by suppressing XRUN metrics or degrading sound.

### Release
Cross-reference #7 full optimization and new v0.6.1 hardware performance issue. Record as a hard P0 gate for next corrective firmware release; preserve v0.6.1 and previous rollbacks, don't alter a concurrent Work publisher. No implementation/passed claim until source, tests and artifacts exist.

title: P0 v0.6.1 AIR UX: Scanning forever, no graphical proximity meter or selectable Kaoss-like effects
body:
## Hardware report, published v0.6.1
Owner reports K1 AIR RADIO stays 'Scanning'; it is impossible to tell whether antenna proximity detection is working or what AIR is controlling. Wants a visible, fast, informative **Kaoss Pad-like live FX controller** (Korg-inspired, original UX). 

**Source facts**: `device/ui.c` case 66 returns `air_on?"Scanning":"Off"` unconditionally; 'Scanning' is **not** proof of real advertisements. AIR page currently prints numeric SIGNAL RAW / PACKETS / WET %, but no large animated meter. `device/app.c` maps AIR K1=radio, K2=target role, K3=calibrate, K4=hold, and `aq_air_update` outputs 0 without a recent calibrated raw signal. No available AIR FX type selector. `vendor/patches/aquora-passive-air.patch` adds passive BLE advertisements/RSSI collection, but physical packet reception is unverified. DSP chiefly changes reverb/send.

**Required**:
- Expose reliable hardware state: RADIO OFF, STARTING, LISTENING / NO BROADCASTER, PACKETS RECEIVED, CALIBRATE FAR, CALIBRATE NEAR, ACTIVE, SIGNAL LOST, RF ERROR, and a packet counter/rate. Distinguish state from an eternally displayed 'Scanning'; never claim actual hand sensing when packets unavailable.
- Prominent animated **raw RSSI / smoothed signal / calibrated 0-100 proximity** bar or motion graph, current target, selected FX type, modulation depth, **actual wet parameter output %**; indicate feedback visually while the hand moves. Use physically observed data, no fake movement.
- Accessible **FX chooser and mapping**: reverb wet, delay wet/feedback/time within safe ranges, filter tone, shimmer/tone if implemented, combinations/presets and a configurable depth; knob navigation should allow selecting FX, target track/all, Hold/Latch/Momentary, sensitivity and calibrate without obscure subpages. Add musical, graceful Kaoss-like response while preserving zero-point baseline and no zipper/click artifacts. Implement only effects supported by actual DSP; no invented XY sensing from 1D RSSI; optional second knob provides explicit X coordinate.
- JIANT-style receive-only ambient radio path, RF calibration safety, auto recovery when transmitters absent, Bluetooth Off near-zero load. Calibrate only after recent valid samples; require real packet rates, sample sensitivity and hand-shadow tests on the FM-1; fallback manual FX knob if sensor unavailable.
- **P0 performance**: no radio starvation/audio crackle; audio first; A/B AIR OFF/ON/active at 16 voices with graphics hidden and displayed; ensure overhead well bounded. Host radio fixtures cannot prove physical hand sensing. 
- On-device Quick Find documentation, 240×240 visual UI captures and owner test checklist. Existing audio balance, 432/440 and binaural separation preserved.
**Status: user cannot verify AIR operation; source confirms misleading label and missing effect chooser.**

comments.body:
## Owner FM-1 test — K3 CALIBRATE switches to READY and remains there (Nov 5, 2026)
Owner attached a photo of AIR screen and reports: turning **K3 CALIBRATE** makes its status remain **"Ready"**, yet there is no clear feedback that proximity is sensing a hand, what FX is being modulated, or whether the radio is receiving signals.

**Verified v0.6.1 source explanation**:
- `device/ui.c`, control 68 displays `air_sensor.calibrated?"Ready":"Turn right"`.
- `device/app.c`, control 68 calls `aq_air_calibrate(&air_sensor,plat_ms())` on positive turn.
- `device/air_sensor.h`: calibrate stores an RSSI reference and sets `calibrated=1` if filtered is nonzero and last signal <800ms. `aq_air_update()` zeros stale `filtered/raw` after 800ms, **but never resets `calibrated`**.
- Thus Ready is only a **latched successful baseline capture indicator**, not proof that the radio remains active, is receiving packets, hand proximity works, or FX output moves. The UI needs **separate CALIBRATED and SIGNAL LIVE statuses**. Do not mislabel successful calibration as continuous AIR readiness.
- K1's 'Scanning' indicates only `air_on`, and `air_packets` is reset each 80ms `plat_air_sample` poll (not a stable cumulative/second packet count). So a '0' can be transient and the current UI provides insufficient evidence.

**Mandatory correction**: visible animated live signal/proximity bar with raw & filtered RSSI trend, packet rate over a stable 1–2s window, last packet age, baseline reference, live 0–100 modulation value, selected FX and actual wet parameter; meaningful states 'LISTENING', 'NO BROADCASTER', 'CALIBRATED – WAITING FOR SIGNAL', 'ACTIVE', 'SIGNAL LOST', 'RADIO ERROR' and explicit manual FX fallback. Add Far/Near guidance and thresholds/hysteresis, signal timeout handling. On loss, show calibrated baseline stored but ***not*** active; smoothly return FX to safe neutral, never stick on last wet unexpectedly except explicit Hold mode. Verify packet path on actual FM-1; initial calibration success may indicate recent RF data, **not** successful hand sensing. Full Korg Kaoss-inspired effect selector/presets still needed. Retain existing audio engine/FX quality and keep radio OFF near-zero cost. Add tests for packet->Ready->timeout->recovery and real hand-shadow response, plus 240x240 captures.

**No implementation made in this comment**; awaits next corrective release.

## Concept expansion: AIR as an intentional, gesture-playable instrument rather than a single reverb slider

Owner requested creative, differentiated ways to **alter, generate, transform and add live FX specifically through FM-1 hand movement**, with uncompromising audio performance. These are proposed designs, **not implemented features or verified gesture capabilities**.

### Design constraint — actual sensor signal
Published v0.6.1 `device/air_sensor.h` receives intermittent ambient Bluetooth packet strength, filters with 0.24 coefficient and computes a 0–100 scalar from far-reference minus current strength. It has **one inferred proximity dimension**, not true XYZ spatial tracking. Fast hand-wave recognition requires sufficient, stable, recent packets; RF multipath may invert movement or make gestures unreliable. The current hand sensor is **not yet owner-validated**. Design fallback to knob control and meaningful state/packet/confidence meter; never simulate actual signal. Do not create a fake two-axis touch sensor.

### 10 purpose-built AIR instrument modes
1. **Ethereal Bloom** — near-hand gradually increases selected-role harmonic brightness, pad/choir presence, and reverb send; return to baseline on retreat. Soft expressive control, no additional voices required.
2. **Celestial Echo Throw** — confident approach/retreat crossing a velocity threshold requests a short tempo-quantized delay-send burst, decays automatically; not an uncontrolled feedback loop. Rate-limit to one gesture per subdivision/phrase as appropriate.
3. **Crystal Hold** — a deliberate, calibrated dwell or explicit HOLD latches a safe sustained FX tail. Can initially reuse bounded reverb/delay feedback; true spectral/time-buffer freeze would require separate feasibility and profiling. Clear unfreeze/release and fail-safe.
4. **Angelic Harmony Conductor** — sustained approach schedules 1–2 harmony/call-and-response events via existing intention/scale-compatible generator, tempo-quantized and bounded, preserving motif identity/locks, not heavy new voices.
5. **Water Crystal Sculptor** — hand movement modulates the **visible** Polar Bloom cymatics-inspired geometry plus existing audio resonance controls; motion and geometry use real musical signals/selected intention/frequency, only when displayed. Do not modify exact reference Hz based on noisy signal.
6. **Living Nature** — approach gently increases current intention/style-appropriate nature ambience level/activity/width within user limits; retreats fade down; never overrides Nature OFF or MANUAL/LOCK.
7. **Rhythm Summoner** — confident gesture requests one musically placed fill or accent from existing drum generator. Cap note density/energy, quantize timing, respect drum OFF/locks; no need for per-sample DSP effect.
8. **Invisible Kaoss Pad** — actual AIR proximity maps to Y; **physical knob or SELECT** maps to X, providing two independent axes without pretending Bluetooth RSSI knows left/right movement. Configurable pairs: reverb/delay, filter tone/send, Nature activity/spatial depth. 240×240 onscreen X-Y marker with labels, real sensor confidence and actual DSP values.
9. **Starlight Arpeggiator** — hover schedules a sparse, scale-constrained arpeggio derived from the currently held/generated chord; release gradually reduces activity. Existing melodic event scheduler, ceiling on extra notes; no fixed-frequency tuning changes.
10. **Breath of the Cosmos** — slow changes smoothly modulate swell, timbral warmth and bounded spatial modulation; reuse existing DSP coefficients/effects instead of adding per-sample oscillators.

### Interaction grammar and musical safety
- Prefer **3 reliable motion primitives** first: APPROACH/RETREAT, STEADY HOVER (dwell), and explicit LATCH/HOLD. Only enable quick flick and double-wave gestures after verifying packet rate, dropout bounds and noise confidence on physical hardware. Short sporadic packets are not sufficient for reliable complex gesture recognition.
- Treat user-selected **AIR preset** (Bloom/Echo/Crystal/Nature/Rhythm etc) as an explicit mode. One canonical settings location, large FX name + selected role + actual wet/output + raw/filtered signal, FAR/NEAR calibration, HOLD, sensitivity and a **LIVE/NO BROADCASTER/SIGNAL LOST** indicator. Offer original panel-based Kaoss-inspired visualization as UI, but AIR hardware measurement remains 1-D.
- Provide simple suggested packages: Serenity (Bloom+Nature), Celestial (Echo+Harmony), Crystal (Freeze+Polar), Rhythm (fill+delay). Defer complex layered effects until baseline hands-on sensing passes.
- No baseline jump: entering AIR snapshots original parameters; all modulation is temporary offsets or dedicated sends that crossfade smoothly back when disabled/lost, preserving manual FX, Nature, patch locks and saved preferences. User can intentionally latch specific output. Avoid random changes to master level, tempo, tonic, 432/440 tuning, binaural L/R, exact fixed/sacred reference frequency and stability.
- Gesture event FX must be beat-aware using existing transport counters; sample-level DSP never sees noisy sensor readouts.

### CPU/MEM optimization acceptance
- Radio reads and proximity/gesture classification at **bounded control rate** (e.g. 10–20 Hz if BLE packet updates genuinely support it), trivial scalar smoothing/hysteresis; no FFT/memory allocation/sensor-driven sin/exp inside audio callback.
- Event-based changes feed already present DSP parameter targets, smoothing at block rate, extra voices/ornaments strictly budgeted; reuse FX send buses/delay/reverb and precomputed curves. No new large real-time buffers without measured benefit. AIR OFF -> radio and optional logic genuinely idle; AIR page hidden -> **UI sensor meter/geometry/graph dormant** while AIR audio control can keep working if enabled.
- Quantified default PLAY A/B tests under **physical v0.6.1 baseline 83% Audio+FX after cold boot, 0 XRUNs in observed window**, plus prior first-post-install 97%/82 XRUN regression. Never trade a gesture effect for audio crackle.
- Host fixtures: steady packet stream, few packets, missing broadcaster, signal reversal, fast spikes, multipath noise, stale calibration, disabled mode, all eight target roles, hold/latch, high drum activity, frozen Nature, exact-Hz/binaural purity, 3h simulation, all preset transitions. Actual FM-1 must verify hand response before saying any mode works.

**Implementation order**: (1) validate receiving signal & reliable proximity meter (#13), (2) Ethereal Bloom and Invisible Kaoss Pad using existing FX only, (3) Celestial Echo Throw and Living Nature, (4) more advanced gesture-to-composition/Crystal modes if real input data supports them. Keep creative design modular; do not bloat the upcoming critical performance hotfix.

title: P1 late-add 0.6.1: compact battery status indicator with automatic fullscreen fade-out
body:
## Owner directive — add to the currently in-progress corrective build (late integration)
Add a **small, readable battery meter/status icon** throughout AQUORA's normal interface. In fullscreen, it should be briefly visible then **fade away completely**, leaving the music visualizer immersive and truly edge-to-edge (see #10). This is a compact, bounded, low-risk late addition **before the final integration tests and release**, not a reason to redo completed work.

### Verified existing platform API
FM1-base `include/plat.h` defines `int plat_battery(void)` with values:
- `-1`: battery state not yet read;
- `0..3`: coarse battery level, from empty to full;
- `4`: powered by USB host (not proof battery is charging).

The published 0.6.0 `device/ui.c` has no `plat_battery` display, and its fullscreen path renders `geometry(band*48)` across all five 240×48 strips. Integrate a tiny icon/status overlay into the existing strip UI path without changing or delaying the audio engine. Do **not** invent a high-precision battery percentage from a 4-step reading.

### User-visible behavior
1. Normal mode: show a compact, attractive battery glyph (four possible levels) in a consistent small top corner where it does not obstruct active controls, with a clear low-battery indicator and a distinct **USB powered** glyph when `plat_battery()==4`.
2. Unknown (`-1`): show a neutral/unknown icon or temporarily omit; never report 0%, charge state, or failure falsely. Avoid displaying spurious battery level during ADC settling.
3. Fullscreen: selected visualizer still fills the entire 240×240 LCD. Battery indicator may appear discreetly for a moment after fullscreen entry, then fade via a short nonblocking 1–3 second stepped-dim transition to **fully invisible** (no persistent blank overlay, header or ghost pixels). Never shrink or letterbox the visualizer to reserve icon space.
4. Low battery: if a supported, trusted status is detected, allow a brief unobtrusive warning/reappearance; do not repeatedly cover the artwork or make unsupported claims about numeric remaining time/percent. If stronger critical warnings are desired, derive reliable capabilities from the hardware driver first.
5. Consistent behavior on PLAY/SOUND/EVOLVE/MIX/DRUMS/SETUP/AIR, menu navigation, enter/exit fullscreen, wake gestures and 10-second auto fullscreen. Don't consume playable keyboard events or alter settings/transport.
6. Poll battery at a bounded UI/control rate only, not inside the audio callback; avoid interfering with key ADC scanning. Re-render only on status/fade changes. Implement fade using inexpensive color palette steps or bounded dithering, not costly per-pixel alpha shaders.
7. Make battery status accessible from a readable status/ABOUT area if the icon would otherwise be ambiguous.

### Acceptance
- Host UI tests for -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4; low/USB state; fullscreen fade sequence; return from fullscreen; no stale pixels or permanent obscuring of edge-to-edge artwork.
- Actual 240×240 normal and fullscreen screenshots (e.g. at entry and 3 seconds later), correct small icon, clean fade and full-screen art occupancy.
- Build/test native + single-core + emulator after integration; compare audio and FPS behavior against current branch; zero audio/FX processing change.
- User verifies physical battery state and LCD behavior on FM-1; not hardware-verified by host tests.

### Concurrent-build safety
AQUORA 0.6.1 development may be underway in another Work environment. **Do not edit shared in-progress source from a separate concurrent worker, replace tags, force-push, or publish from two environments.** The **single active release builder** should read this issue, implement it near final UI integration, and include it in the 0.6.1 final acceptance matrix. - [`device/ui.c`](https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/blob/v0.6.0/device/ui.c): fullscreen already draws five 240×48 strips of `geometry(band*48)`, correctly allocating the **full framebuffer area**, but geometry **occupancy** is not controlled by fullscreen bounds and can leave visually small/underwhelming subjects.

These restricted coordinate ranges help explain why a fullscreen mode can technically draw all bands while the actual visual doesn't use the screen's height/edges.
- [`device/app.c`](https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/blob/v0.6.0/device/app.c) automatically enters fullscreen after 10s PLAY inactivity; knob/button activity exits it, while keys can still play. Preserve these behaviors unless changed by owner.

Occupy the screen with immersive geometry, dynamic edges, volumetric depth/tilt, background texture, restrained particles and beautiful lighting; preserve visual focal point and avoid cropping the central composition. A scene can have deliberate negative space, but not an accidental letterboxed/miniature visualizer.

Center main focus visually around ~(120,120), with meaningful details across the full area. 5. Progressive rendering and safe clipping: efficient 240×48 LCD strip draw, fixed vertex/particle budgets, correct coordinate transforms, no bands/tearing artifacts, no stale pixels after entering/exiting or selecting presets. Do not add costly per-pixel glow/FFT; optimize along with issue #7.

title: P0: EVOLVE must drive sustained nonrepeating musical development across all intentions and 8 roles
body:
## Owner hardware requirement — mandatory corrective release
**EVOLVE cannot merely show a variation percentage or occasional random notes.** The user should be able to set EVOLVE controls and hear genuinely creative, harmonious, constantly renewing musical development over long sessions while maintaining song identity and each intention's style. Changes in EVOLVE must be audible and traceable on the requested animated real-time EVOLVE graph ([issue #4](https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/issues/4)).

## Source audit
Published [v0.6.0 `device/dsp/engine.c`](https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/blob/v0.6.0/device/dsp/engine.c) `trigger()` has probabilistic phrase changes gated by `e->variation`, `e->freeze`, absolute step/loop boundary, plus section/phrase choices. But this is **not proof** of coherent sustained progression/anti-repetition for all 8 roles or meaningful distinct control over macro musical development. `device/ui.c` exposes VARIATION, ENERGY and FREEZE; current EVOLVE tabs are LOOP/EDIT, NEW SONG/EDIT, GROOVE/EDIT. The preexisting `NEXT_BUILD_ACTIVE.md` explicitly calls for 3–8 hour music progression and accessible evolution controls; audit any implementation already done rather than repeating it.

## Required capabilities
1. Clear EVOLVE panel with immediately discoverable controls: **EVOLUTION LEVEL = Stable / Subtle / Flowing / Adventurous**, variation intensity, **SECTION / PHRASE** display, pace of change, optional role Hold/Follow/Evolve, Freeze/Unfreeze, next variation / next section, 16/32/64 loops. Explain differences in plain language.
2. **Macro evolution**: multi-minute changing arrangements, intro/build/resolve/rest/return, textural density, evolving energy and intentional breakdowns/rebuilds; coherent with the chosen intention, instrument role patch, drum kit and nature/FX palette. Never let progression be just a repeated 16-step phrase with occasional random pitch substitutions.
3. **Meso evolution**: motifs remembered, transformed, variation/repeat, call-and-response, complementary evolving piano/arps/chords and changing bass/drum patterns; frequent enough to hear, paced by selectable evolution level and current intention.
4. **Micro evolution**: subtle accents, velocities, note spacing, timbral motion and phrase articulation that are restrained when the mode is Stable or low-energy. Higher intensity must create meaningfully more musical variation, not simply loudness, density or random key changes.
5. **All 8 roles** (Lead, Bass, Pads/Drone, Harmony, Piano, Plucks, Choir and Drums) must evolve distinctly and musically. Bass moves beyond repeating tonic, drum patterns/fills/ghost hits evolve without unintended aggressive percussion, pads/choir morph chord/entrance, melodies build recognizable leitmotifs.
6. **Intention/style awareness**: keep musical identity, corresponding patches/kits/Nature/FX, scale, 432/440, chosen reference HZ and binaural channel separation stable. Never change exact reference frequencies. Respect all track locks, manually selected patches/kits, Nature Auto/Manual/Off, Freeze, solo/mute and saved banks. EVOLVE must not unilaterally reset style or override user decisions.
7. **Long-session memory**: bounded fixed-size motif/section/drum/bass histories to avoid obvious repetition, allow motifs to return after meaningful variation. Deterministic reproducible seed behavior, sensible 16/32/64-step structure and seamless transitions, no hung notes or endlessly increasing memory; save/restore the evolution state where appropriate.
8. **Real-time EVOLVE graph:** animate actual section/phrase state, role activity, bass/drum changes, requested/observed motif transformations, upcoming transitions and Freeze/Lock; every knob adjustment visibly changes its accurate model, with audible result. No fake graphs or frozen generic art.
9. **Tests**: multi-seed, every 13 intentions, all 8 roles, all loop lengths, all evolution levels incl zero and freeze, dynamic patch/kit/nature/style changes, New Song/Reroll Sounds semantics, manual locks, stop/start, 3–8-hour accelerated simulation and long PCM listening checks. Measure event-sequence uniqueness, motif retention/recall, section diversity, CPU/FX p95/p99 and XRUN delta. Verify 0% or Stable actually produces stable patterns, higher intensities demonstrate meaningfully more evolution without chaos.
10. Preserve beautiful existing musical balance and optimize performance using low-cost control-rate scheduling, **not per-sample additional algorithmic cost**. Cross-reference optimisation #7, sound library #6, UI #2.

## Evidence and release
Create a concise before/after timeline of musical changes per role, A/B listening samples for every evolution level, animated EVOLVE emulator recordings and hardware test checklist. Hardware artistic acceptance belongs to owner. Complete in next versioned corrective release without modifying published 0.6.0.

title: P0: Audible 8-second AQUORA intro with original FM cinematic startup inspired by PlayStation 1
body:
## Owner's updated November 5, 2026 hardware feedback — overrides previous Game Boy concept
The owner hears **no intro sound effect** when starting AQUORA v0.6.1. They now want a memorable **original, ambient FM-synthesized startup inspired by the spacious, mysterious, cinematic feel of the Sony PlayStation 1 boot experience**, rather than the prior Game Boy-style chime. Keep the intro **8 seconds**, visually display the saved visualizer and selected panel theme, and instantly skip on any knob/button/key.

This supersedes the old Game Boy sound reference completely. Compose **new music and sound design**, not a copy of Sony's protected startup recording, distinctive melody, or exact sonic sequence.

### Source-confirmed investigation starting point (published v0.6.1)
- `device/app.c::app_render()` contains an intro `bell` generated with **two high sine partials** using `fm_sinf(t*2764.6015f)` and `fm_sinf(t*4160.1589f)`, with ~3s `intro_samples` gate, amplitude multiplied by `intro_gain` and `output_gain`. It is a tiny stereo-identical bell, **not an actual multioperator FM-ambient orchestration**, and may be barely audible in the actual speaker chain.
- `intro_samples` counts sample frames and stops after 3s even though intro visuals run 10s in actual published v0.6.1. `app_input_only()` still uses `now-intro_start>=10000u`; issue #8's 8s request is **not implemented yet**.
- `output_gain` follows the physical `master` value and resets to zero at master=0; `intro_gain` also becomes zero at master=0. Check whether inaudibility is caused by master volume, first startup audio/DMA initialization, timing (3s chime expired before ready), routing/codec/speaker/headphones, mute, amplitude, accidental skip or another actual bug. **Do not assert a diagnosis before testing**.
- Current bell has **no true FM operator modulation**, no evolving low tone, no spatial motion or ambient tail, and does **per-audio-sample `fm_sinf`** calls. Given reported default v0.6.1 overload immediately after flash, new intro must be extremely cheap and isolated from the general 16-voice instrument engine during startup.

### Required new sonic identity — self-composed, FM-native, 8 seconds maximum
- A low, soft, mysterious **FM shimmer and resonant swelling chord** rises out of near-silence; gentle harmonic metallic/glass tones bloom into an original signature interval/motif; warm diffuse airy tail resolves peacefully into AQUORA. A sense of scale and wonder, but characteristically **AQUORA's own unique brand identity**, not an audio replica of PlayStation, Sony, Nintendo, or another startup.
- Within 8s with clear presence on the FM-1 speaker **and** headphones at normal listening volume. Do not rely on deep subbass inaudible on tiny speakers; include balanced midrange, smooth harmonics and sensible levels. Remain refined, never an aggressive blast.
- Use existing sine LUT / very lightweight 2-op FM phase accumulation, 2–4 bounded voices max, control-rate envelopes, precomputed coefficients and extremely cheap stereo widening appropriate to hardware; no new large PCM asset or reverb buffers. A subtle lightweight single-tap stereo tail or efficient reuse of available stable send path; never initialize full expensive effects solely for the intro.
- Separate **intro elapsed time** (wall-clock ~8s) from **audio start time** (when the audio pipeline is actually ready). Trigger a clearly audible onset once output is ready and fit the motif into the remaining intro window instead of wasting its first seconds during device initialization; avoid playing late after user skips.
- Seamless synchronization with visual startup (current Original or Polar Bloom preference), matching swells to crystal/geometry blooms without expensive continuous extra geometry or background telemetry.

### Physical controls and safety
- **Skippable immediately** by *any knob, button, or key*, consume skip input to prevent accidental transport/patch changes or surprise notes; graceful ~20–80ms audio fade, no pops or leaked FX after skip. Stay compatible with watchdog/recovery/update startup.
- Honor **hardware master = 0 as silence**, and an optional saved Startup Chime OFF / Quiet / Normal setting that is obvious and not duplicated elsewhere. Do not force sound when user explicitly muted, and never start with unsafe fixed high output volume. Provide clear on-device option to enable/disable. Avoid accidental skip due to jitter in analog master-reading unless there was an intentional input edge.
- Store overall 8-second intro duration and startup setting correctly with versioned migration, preserving existing settings/LED/banks/visualizer theme; no per-frame flash writes.

### Acceptance/tests before next corrective release
1. Programmatically capture the **actual device PCM/DAC feed** from startup after device init and verify nonzero expected waveform on active volume, not merely a simulated oscillator, across master level settings, speaker vs headphones routing and audio pipeline startup timing; verify zero samples when muted.
2. A/B test v0.6.1 current intro vs new FM intro for loudness (safe peak/RMS), audible midband content, envelope shape, absence of DC/clipping, predictable 8s duration, graceful skip/fade under every input, and no post-intro audio tail/leak.
3. Provide a short listenable WAV from the exact firmware synthesis path and emulator startup video preview with audio, with test results attached to GitHub Actions.
4. Compare CPU overhead and callback p95/p99, first-boot-after-install performance, extra FX use, XRUN delta vs no-intro, and memory. **No regression to default PLAY** (#12).
5. Physical FM-1 speaker/headphones sound acceptance remains **owner-unverified** until tested; cite only verified software evidence.

### Scope and relationship
Update the intro feature tracked in this issue instead of adding another overlapping issue. Keep selected visualizer persisted (#16), styled panel themes (#16), visible fullscreen recovery (#14), hidden graphics gating (#15), post-install first PLAY issue (#12), optimization (#7). Work's next versioned corrective release must include this before declaring intro complete. Do not modify published v0.6.1 or any in-progress concurrent Work checkout. Status: **requested, not implemented**.

title: P0: Full-project optimization, deduplication and safe cleanup before next corrective release
body:
## Owner directive — mandatory whole-project optimization pass (next AQUORA corrective build)

During this corrective build, perform an **end-to-end optimization, deduplication and safe cleanup pass** across the entire firmware project: source code, DSP/music generation, FM synthesis, drum engine, Nature Beds, FX, visualizers, dynamic SOUND/EVOLVE graphs, UI/navigation, LEDs, BLE/AIR, memory, assets, toolchains and build/release files. Remove code/assets/dependencies that are provably obsolete, unused, redundant or duplicated. Do **not** delete historical GitHub backups, published release assets, recovery/update tooling, licensed notices, or any reachable functionality simply because it looks old.

**Optimization is part of acceptance, not an optional later pass. Preserve all features the owner likes and the new requirements tracked in issues #1–#6.**

### 1 — Establish a reproducible baseline
- Start from the latest verified GitHub source and tagged published 0.6.0 baseline; use isolated GitHub Actions runners, not the blocked shared Work lock. Confirm a single release publisher.
- Record firmware/source SHA and binary sizes, flash sections, RAM/data/bss/stack/static buffers, free headroom, real callback costs at 44.1 kHz / 256 frames (~5805 µs), audio/FX p50/p95/p99/max, XRUN delta, clip/limiter stats, visual frame/geometry/update times, single-core fallbacks, and artifact sizes.
- Profile representative scenarios: idle/playing; 1 vs 16 voices; dense drums; Nature OFF/Forest/Birds/new beds; binaural and fixed-frequency lock; AIR OFF/idle/modulating; each visualizer including new Vizz-inspired mode; editing live SOUND and EVOLVE graphs; keys/LED dance; save/restore and USB/updater activity.
- Attribute hotspots to actual functions before rewriting, and distinguish host benchmark proxies from delivered FM-1 performance.

### 2 — CPU/DSP, FX and generator
- Refactor heavy per-sample work into cached values, lookup/interpolation, control-rate updates, preplanned steps/events where **audibly and numerically equivalent**; minimize repeated trig, exp, divisions, branches, redundant mixer passes, denormal work and excess voice/FX processing.
- Reuse effects buses/shared processing where valid; keep independent source routing and mute/solo accurate; gate or bypass inactive effects, Nature, radio, graphics and visual telemetry at **near-zero incremental cost when OFF**.
- Preserve high-quality intention-aware melodies, patch and kit choices, dynamic evolution, naturalistic ambience, binaural stereo isolation, strict reference-Hz purity, tuning, tempo, Play Along, envelope transitions, musical balance and anti-click behavior.
- Profile new lightweight 2-op FM paths / resonant percussion and realistic procedural/compact-sample Nature Beds so they do not overwhelm audio. Never silently reduce sound quality or delete unique usable patches in the name of optimization.

### 3 — Memory, graphics, UI and LED handling
- Bound buffers and reduce duplicate tables, recomputation and temporary copies; check worst-case RAM/stack and overflow bounds on FM1 hardware targets.
- Optimize the Original and newly requested second Vizz-inspired visualizers: fixed-bounded vertex/particle counts, cached geometry, efficient depth ordering/projection, dirty rectangles/partial LCD updates where safe, no excessive memory bandwidth, core-1 worker where hardware validated and safe core-0 fallback.
- The live SOUND/EVOLVE audio-accurate graphs must use **bounded, decimated, lock-free telemetry** rather than heavy DSP copies or fake motion. Keep UI editable/responsive under max load; graph OFF must not incur ongoing cost.
- Implement efficient LED event update masks/brightness and music-reactive Dance mode with low CPU/power burden; fix On mode and no stuck state.

### 4 — Code, build, asset and dependency cleanup
- Build an inventory of reachable modules/controls/assets, duplicate helpers/tables, unused debug/test-only production code, unused images/audio, dead branches, stale docs, obsolete build outputs, redundant archives, risky macro/constant duplication and unreferenced dependencies.
- Verify reachability via build/linker maps, source references, firmware feature matrix and emulator UI paths **before removing any production file or symbol**. Archive or retain test fixtures needed for regression. Respect GPL/MPL/third-party attribution and pinned SDK provenance.
- Replace duplicated logic with one well-tested implementation where practical; use clean interfaces and ensure compile-time/runtime feature flags behave consistently in native, forced single-core, host emulator, and recovery/installer builds.
- Prune **only generated or genuinely obsolete build products from the active tree**, never historical GitHub releases or source backups without explicit owner instruction.
- Maintain accurate, short current build queue and release docs: do not mark work complete on intention alone; cite changed files, tests and measured improvements.

### 5 — Required validation and proof
- Run incremental targeted tests while optimizing, then **full final acceptance** against all features and issue #1–#6 requirements. Include reproducible A/B PCM audio and output behavior comparisons, deterministic song selection/locks/migrations, Nature/FX stereo/level checks, over-time evolution, old/new UI control navigation/mutation, LED outputs, BLE/AIR simulated paths, save/load, release updater, native and forced single-core, WASM/emulator, installer and long-duration stress.
- Supply a compact *before/after scorecard* with CPU/audio/FX p95/p99, XRUN delta, flash/RAM/binary size, graphics work/frame timing and artifacts. Do not claim improvement where data is missing; call out tradeoffs.
- Any cleanup that causes audio artifacts, missed LCD updates, altered tuning, inaccessible controls, bank incompatibility, update failure or other regression must be reverted or fixed.
- Final target is **measurably leaner and more stable** with maximum verified headroom, not simply fewer lines of code; do not invent a performance gain. Hardware AIR responsiveness, delivered LCD FPS, DMA stability, physical LED behavior, physical-key feel and sound quality await owner's FM-1 verification.
- Preserve published v0.6.0 and v0.5.0 rollback. Publish the next versioned corrective release **only after** matching code, tests, archives, checksums and live installer are verified.

## Execution style
Work in coherent batches with independent reproducible GitHub Actions; avoid old shared lock and wasted duplicate testing; checkpoint compactly to GitHub. No need to stop at intermediate subgoals. Mark this issue complete **only after an optimization report and end-to-end verified release artifacts exist**.
